props.gloss_en: R' Eliezer (mishna): one may pour into a suspended strainer on Shabbat
Chachamim (mishna lemma): one may not pour into a suspended strainer on Shabbat
Rav Kahana: one who strained [wine] is liable to a sin-offering
Rav Sheshet: there is nothing for which the Rabbis impose a sin-offering while R' Eliezer permits it ab initio
a woman may not go out with a city of gold
R' Meir: and if she went out, she is liable to a sin-offering
Chachamim: she may not go out, and if she went out she is exempt
R' Eliezer: a woman may go out with a city of gold ab initio
R' Eliezer's 'ab initio' is said against R' Meir, who imposes a sin-offering
Abaye: R' Eliezer is responding to the Rabbis, who say exempt but forbidden, and he tells them it is permitted ab initio
Rabba: [one who strains is warned] on account of selecting
R' Zeira: [one who strains is warned] on account of sifting
Rabba: the way of selecting is to take the food and leave the waste; so too here, one takes the food and leaves the waste
R' Zeira: the way of sifting is waste above and food below; so too here, waste above and food below
a doubled cloak -- one may not make [it into a covering]; if he did, he is exempt but it is forbidden
if a string or cord was wound on it, it may be spread ab initio
Rav (asked about a canopy): even a bed is forbidden
Rav (asked about a bed): even a canopy is permitted
Rav (asked about canopy and bed): the canopy is forbidden
Rav (same answer): and the bed is permitted
where he said 'even a bed is forbidden' -- [beds] like the Carmanians'
where he said 'even a canopy is permitted' -- as Rami bar Yechezkel [taught: with a string wound on it]
'a canopy is forbidden and a bed permitted' -- [canopies and beds] like ours
Rav Yosef: I saw the canopies of Rav Huna's house -- in the evening spread out, and in the morning cast down lying
a curtain may be spread and may be dismantled
a grooms' canopy may be spread and may be dismantled
this was said only where its roof is not a handbreadth wide; if it is, it is forbidden
and even without a handbreadth roof, only where there is no handbreadth [of width] within three of its roof; if there is, it is forbidden
and only where its slope has no handbreadth; if it does, [it is forbidden]
the slopes of tents are like tents
and only where it does not descend a handbreadth below the bed; if it does, it is forbidden

כדרמי בר יחזקאל -- the case where a string was wound on it, which his baraita permits ab initio
שיפועי אהלים כאהלים דמו -- a handbreadth of slope counts as a tent's roof

challenges.gloss_en: מתקיף לה רב ששת: מי איכא מידי דרבנן מחייבי חטאת ורבי אליעזר שרי לכתחילה?! -- if straining is a sin-offering, the mishna's Chachamim (who forbid pouring into a suspended strainer) would impose a sin-offering where R' Eliezer permits ab initio; no answer is given, and the sugya goes on to ask under which melacha the strainer is warned

objections.gloss_en: מתקיף לה רב יוסף: אלמה לא? הרי עיר של זהב, דרבי מאיר מחייב חטאת ורבי אליעזר שרי לכתחילה -- the baraita is supplied by the stam (מאי היא -- דתניא, 138a.6)

answered_by.gloss_en: מי סברת רבי אליעזר אדרבי מאיר קאי? אדרבנן קאי, דאמרי פטור אבל אסור -- R' Eliezer's 'ab initio' answers the intermediate 'exempt but forbidden', not the sin-offering (= p_re_kai_aderabanan)
